model: Regulated utility dividend capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: management guidance: 6-8% non-GAAP operating EPS CAGR 2025-2030 on 6.0-7.5% rate-base growth; base path lands at 6.4% (FY2030E $5.53 on FY2025 $4.05)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-year CAGR (1.2%) diverges more than 30% from revenue (4.8%) and EPS (2.3%) and is not usable as the growth anchor: FY2021 carried a ~$2.7bn pre-tax impairment on the fossil generation fleet sold in 2022 plus a $500M buyback, cutting equity from $15,984M to $14,438M. The 3-year EPS CAGR (27%) is equally distorted by FY2022 mark-to-market losses (GAAP EPS $2.06). Rate-base growth and the operating-EPS guidance are the meaningful anchors.
historical_growth.notes: FY2025 vs FY2022 and FY2020, GAAP figures from the Metrics CSV. Owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC) is negative at both ends of each window (FY2025 -$17M, FY2022 -$1,414M, FY2020 $144M to -$17M), so no FCF CAGR is meaningful; this is the rate-base investment cycle, not distress. SBC is ~0.35% of revenue and immaterial to the trend. Dividends per share grew $2.52 (FY2025) to $2.68 (FY2026 indicative), +6.3%.

scenario_narratives.base: PSE&G executes roughly the midpoint of its $22.5-25.5bn regulated programme, rate base compounds at ~6.75% from $36bn, and the formula transmission rate, GSMP III and CEF-EE clauses keep regulatory lag short. Operating EPS grows 6.4% a year to about $5.53 in 2030, just inside the 6-8% guide, after a soft 2027 that absorbs the Salem 1 thermal-shield repair and the loss of the 50bp RTO adder. The plan is funded without common equity and the dividend grows in line with earnings at a ~61.5% payout. PSEG Power earns steady margins above the PTC floor on a hedged book; when the PTC expires after 2032 growth steps down, and the business fades to a 3.5% grower by the mid-2030s with a 65% payout.
scenario_narratives.bull: New Jersey's large-load pipeline converts: multi-gigawatt data-centre interconnections push the capital plan to the $28bn upper end and rate-base growth to 7.5%, while the BPU keeps supporting investment because new load spreads fixed costs. PSEG Power signs a long-term contract for nuclear output at a premium to the PTC floor, as Constellation, Vistra and Talen have, and the Salem uprates and licence renewals proceed. PJM capacity prices hold near the cap. EPS compounds at the top of the 6-8% range to about $5.88 in 2030 and fades slowly.
scenario_narratives.bear: The single-regulator dependency bites. The governor's affordability directives and the BPU's utility business-model study end in lower allowed ROEs, slower clause recovery or bill credits; the transmission adder goes; bad-debt expense stays elevated under the disconnection moratorium. Salem 1's thermal-shield damage keeps the unit out for most of 2027, and correlated inspection findings at Salem 2 are a risk. PJM market redesign and Treasury's gross-receipts guidance cap nuclear upside, and the PTC floor lapses after 2032 into weaker power prices. EPS growth runs at ~4%, below guidance, and funding the programme beyond 2030 requires common equity.

valuation_philosophy.summary: PSEG is valued as a stream of dividends funded by regulated earnings on a growing rate base, discounted at a 7.75% cost of equity, not as a free-cash-flow business: unlevered FCF is consumed by rate-base investment by design. Value is driven by three things only: the per-share earnings growth the capital plan delivers, the payout, and the spread between the cost of equity and long-run growth. The merchant nuclear fleet is inside consolidated earnings rather than valued as a separate option. The 15% hurdle entry price sits at well under half of intrinsic value; that is the cost of demanding 15% from a ~6% grower yielding 3.5%, not a model fault.
key_risks_to_valuation: Discount-rate sensitivity: with a 4.75-point spread between cost of equity and terminal growth, each 0.5 point on the cost of equity moves value by roughly 10%.
New Jersey regulatory and political risk: a single BPU decision on allowed ROE or cost recovery reprices ~80-85% of earnings.
Salem 1 thermal-shield degradation: repair timeline and cost undisclosed; base assumes a one-year drag, bear assumes most of 2027.
Nuclear PTC expiry after 2032 and unresolved Treasury gross-receipts guidance; merchant earnings carry the same multiple as regulated earnings in this model, which flatters them if PJM prices fall.

Funding: the no-new-equity commitment covers 2026-2030 only. Retained earnings (~$0.8bn a year) cover well under the equity share of ~$2.5bn annual rate-base growth, so holding-company leverage is rising; equity issuance after 2030 would dilute per-share growth.
FY0 rests on a guidance midpoint ($4.34) for a year not yet reported, and on non-GAAP operating earnings that exclude mark-to-market and decommissioning-trust swings.
Timing convention: end-of-year discounting with FY2027 as year 1 understates value by ~3-4% relative to actual dividend timing.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 66.15-87.63
data_sources.financials: PEG_Metrics.csv / PEG.duckdb (SEC XBRL); Q3-2026 10-Q (PEG_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt) for the 2026-09-30 balance sheet, cover-page share count at 2026-10-20, diluted share bridge, 9M cash flow and the $2.68 indicative dividend; FY2025 10-K for rate base, capital plan and SBC
data_sources.qualitative: PEG_Analysis.json (2026-11-15): FY2026 operating EPS guidance $4.28-$4.40, 6-8% EPS CAGR 2025-2030, 6.0-7.5% rate-base CAGR, Salem 1 outage, NJ regulatory developments

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement / Note 17 (Stock Based Compensation), $43M; no separate equity-award withholding-tax line is disclosed, so the add-back is used as is. Memo only: SBC is already inside the operating EPS this model capitalises.
inputs.share_count_basis: 498.515M shares outstanding at 2026-10-20 (Q3-2026 10-Q cover) plus ~1M dilutive stock-based awards (Q3-2026 10-Q EPS note: 498 basic / 499 diluted weighted) = 499.5M fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed inside EPS, PSEG has repurchased nothing since the $500M programme of 2022, and management states the 2026-2030 capital plan is funded without new common equity. Equity issuance after 2030 is a bear-case axis, modelled there as slower per-share growth rather than a rising count.
inputs.wacc_rationale: The discount rate is a COST OF EQUITY (the flow is dividends, after interest), built in USD: ~4.3% 10-year Treasury + ~0.7 beta x 5.0% equity risk premium = ~7.75%. Beta sits above a pure wires utility (~0.55-0.6) because 15-20% of earnings come from merchant nuclear generation selling into PJM. Folder precedents: CMS 7.5% (pure regulated), NI 8.25% (genco build-out with equity issuance). The rate is below PSE&G's allowed ROE (9.6% distribution, 9.9% + 50bp adder transmission), which is why a utility earning its allowed return trades above book. One rate for all three scenarios; risk is carried in the scenario paths and weights, not in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable on this route: operating leases are $131M and lease cost is already inside EPS. lease_cost_pct_path left at zero.
inputs.nci_treatment: No non-controlling interest; EPS is wholly attributable to PSEG common.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE. PSEG is a rate-regulated electric and gas T&D utility (PSE&G, ~$36bn rate base, roughly 80-85% of earnings) with a merchant nuclear overlay (PSEG Power, ~3,758 MW in PJM). The dcf-methods routing table has no utility row; its governing principle is to discount the flow the business actually produces at the rate appropriate to whom it accrues, and it warns that reported FCF is structurally negative for infrastructure in a capex supercycle without that being a signal. Reported FCF (OCF - capex) was $26M in FY2025, -$1,247M in FY2024 and -$173M TTM to 2026-09-30, and stays near or below zero through the $24-28bn 2026-2030 plan by design: every dollar enters rate base and earns an allowed return. A firm-level owner-FCF DCF would therefore rest wholly on a terminal value after a guessed capex normalisation, and (as documented on CMS) discounts sub-WACC book returns while ignoring that equity earns the allowed ROE through regulatory leverage. The flow that reaches shareholders is the dividend, so the model capitalises dividends per share at the cost of equity through the Drivers engine with net debt at zero -- the same engine route as NI and the REIT AFFO capitalisations, and consistent with the FCFE-at-cost-of-equity pattern used on CMS/AEE/ED. Because PSEG neither issues nor repurchases common stock, FCFE to shareholders equals the dividend. The merchant nuclear arm is NOT valued separately: its earnings are inside the consolidated operating EPS and its risk is expressed in the scenario growth paths (PTC floor through 2032, PJM capacity prices, Salem 1) and a slightly higher cost of equity than a pure wires utility. ENGINE MAPPING (read the dashboard sliders with this key): 'revenue' = non-GAAP operating earnings to common (EPS x flat 499.5M shares); 'EBITDA margin' 100%; capex_pct = earnings RETENTION (100 - dividend payout); D&A, cash tax, SBC, lease and working capital all 0 because EPS is already after every one of them; 'FCF' = common dividends. net_debt is 0 because the flow is post-interest -- actual debt is $25,634M (long-term $24,134M + current maturities $425M + commercial paper $1,075M) against $837M cash at 2026-09-30, recorded in total_debt/cash for audit only and never deducted. FY0 IS THE GUIDANCE YEAR. base_revenue = FY2026 non-GAAP operating EPS guidance midpoint $4.34 ($4.28-$4.40, reaffirmed 2026-11-02 with Q3 results) x 499.5M = $2,167.8M; FY2025 actual was $4.05 operating / $4.22 GAAP. Year 1 is FY2027, discounted one full year from the valuation date under the house end-of-year convention; FY2027 dividends actually arrive on average about 0.6 years out, and the Q4-2026 dividend of $0.67 (declared, payable around year-end) is excluded entirely, so the timing convention understates value by roughly 3-4%. GAAP earnings are not used as the base because PSEG Power's results swing with non-trading mark-to-market and nuclear decommissioning trust gains (9M-2026 GAAP EPS $2.91 vs $3.59, Q3 $0.76 vs $1.24, against operating EPS of $1.15 in Q3, +2%). OWNER-FCF MEMO: last_fcf = TTM reported FCF -$173M (FY2025 $26M + 9M-2026 $235M - 9M-2025 $434M) less FY2025 SBC $43M = -$216M; it is recorded for auditability and is NOT the base of this model. interest_income is 0 (heavily net-debt). HOUSE vs STREET: SBC is 0.35% of revenue and already expensed inside EPS, so the two bases coincide and the band collapses; band_position carries no information here. BUYBACKS: none since 2022; the flat count is real, not a convention. Book value per share at 2026-09-30 is $34.83 ($17,362M equity), so FY2026E operating ROE is ~12.6% on average equity; terminal retention of 35% x a 9-10% earned ROE supports the 3.0% terminal growth without new equity. Price is a regular-session close, not an after-hours print.

bear.growth_note: FY2027 +1%: Salem 1 is out for most of the year and the transmission adder is lost. FY2028-FY2030 4-4.5% (FY2030E ~$4.99, 4.3% CAGR on FY2025, below the guided range): New Jersey's affordability agenda trims allowed returns or stretches recovery lag on the capital programmes, and the capital plan runs at the low end. FY2033 +2% as the PTC floor lapses into a softer PJM price environment; after 2030 growth needs common equity, expressed here as lower per-share growth.
bear.capex_note: Payout drifts up from 63% to 67% because the dividend is defended while EPS growth lags; the dividend still grows only ~2-4% a year.
bear.terminal_note: Gordon at 7.75% / 2.5% = 19.5x the terminal dividend (~13x earnings); Gordon binds.

base.growth_note: Per-share operating EPS, FY2027-FY2036. FY2027 +5.5% to $4.58: below the 6-8% algorithm for the Salem 1 thermal-shield repair (extended outage, cost and timing undisclosed) and the likely loss of the 50bp transmission RTO adder (~$40M, ~$0.08/share) once NJ's mandatory-RTO-membership law takes effect in January 2027. FY2028-FY2030 +6.5%, giving FY2030E $5.53 = 6.4% CAGR on FY2025's $4.05, the lower-middle of the 6-8% guide and consistent with the midpoint of 6.0-7.5% rate-base growth with no equity issuance. FY2031-32 6.0/5.5% as the current plan rolls into a successor programme; FY2033 4.5% when the nuclear PTC floor expires after 2032; fading to 3.5% by FY2035.
base.capex_note: capex_pct is earnings retention = 100 - dividend payout. FY2026 payout is 61.8% ($2.68 on $4.34). Held at 61.5% through FY2030 (FY2027E dividend $2.82, +5.1%), then rising to 65% by FY2035 as growth slows and less retention is needed.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 7.75% / 3.0% = 21.7x the terminal dividend, about 14x terminal earnings at a 65% payout. The cap is on the dividend flow: 28x dividends = ~18x earnings, the sector's long-run P/E. Gordon binds.

bull.growth_note: Top of the 6-8% algorithm through 2030 (FY2030E ~$5.88, 7.7% CAGR on FY2025) and a slower fade after: capital plan at the $28bn upper end on multi-gigawatt large-load interconnections, a long-term nuclear power sale to a data-centre customer priced above the PTC floor, Salem uprates (~200 MW) and licence renewals, and PJM capacity prices that stay at or near the cap.
bull.capex_note: Slightly higher retention (payout ~60%) while the larger capital plan is funded internally, converging on the same 65% terminal payout.
bull.terminal_note: Gordon at 7.75% / 3.5% = 24.4x the terminal dividend (~16x earnings); below the 28x cap, Gordon binds.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 28x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25%, above the 15% house default: essentially all regulated earnings depend on one state whose new administration has explicitly directed the BPU to mitigate rate increases and study reform of the utility model, and an unresolved nuclear outage with no disclosed repair timeline sits on top. Base 50%: guidance was reaffirmed three times in 2026 and the capital programmes are largely approved or formula-driven. Bull 25%, below the 35% default: it needs both a cooperative regulator at the top of the capital range and a nuclear offtake contract that has been discussed for two years without being signed.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
